cases.about: Proxen SR (naproxen) is supplied three times from March to May 2026 while Eliquis (apixaban) is supplied every month, and the supplies overlap.
Orudis (ketoprofen) was last supplied in February 2026 and Pradaxa (dabigatran) was first supplied in June, more than 60 days later, so the two never overlapped.
Betaloc (metoprolol) and Cardizem CD (diltiazem) are both supplied every month from April to June 2026, overlapping throughout.
Anselol (atenolol) was last supplied in March 2026 and Isoptin SR (verapamil) was first supplied in July, more than 60 days later.

Spiractin (spironolactone) is supplied with monthly Prexum (perindopril) from April 2026, and the record holds a serum potassium result from September 2025, more than six months before the newest supply.
Spiractin is supplied with monthly Atacand (candesartan), and the record holds a serum potassium result from June 2026, within the last six months.
Xarelto (rivaroxaban) is supplied monthly and a course of Kalixocin (clarithromycin) in May 2026 falls within 60 days of the rivaroxaban supplies.
Aratac (amiodarone) was last supplied in February 2026 and Eliquis (apixaban) was first supplied in June, more than 60 days later.
Reminyl (galantamine) is supplied every month from March 2026 together with Sotab (sotalol), and the supplies overlap.
Mestinon (pyridostigmine) is the only medicine of the two groups supplied; there is no beta-blocker, digoxin, diltiazem or verapamil.
OxyNorm (oxycodone) is supplied monthly from March to June 2026 for regular use, and no laxative of any kind is supplied.
Palexia SR (tapentadol) is supplied with Movicol (macrogol) supplied within 60 days of each opioid supply.
Normison (temazepam) is supplied four times from March to June 2026, more than 28 days of supplies in all.
Ralozam (alprazolam) is supplied once, 20 tablets for use no more than twice a week, covering far less than 28 days.
Syquet (quetiapine) and Risperdal (risperidone), two antipsychotics from one class, are both supplied monthly from April 2026, overlapping.
Only Syquet (quetiapine) of the antipsychotic class is supplied; no second medicine of the same class appears.
Physiotens (moxonidine), a centrally-acting antihypertensive, is supplied three times from May 2026.
Coversyl (perindopril) and a diuretic are supplied; neither is a centrally-acting antihypertensive.
Trexject (methotrexate) is supplied three times and the most recent directions say only "Take as directed", with no word of once weekly.
Methoblastin (methotrexate) is supplied monthly and every supply says to take one tablet once a week.
